messages.comparison:
## Fields and pagination across endpoints

- **Work IDs** — Gallery `artworkId` and export `ids[]` use JSON integers such as `42`. Task `workId`, Pixiv search `id` and batch item `key.id` use strings such as `"42"`. Submit illustrations with `workType="artwork"`. The receipt’s `queueType="illust"` names the queue.
- **Download options** — A single task takes string values in `options`. A batch takes JSON booleans or integers for the same settings in `definition.download`. Both request bodies appear below.
- **Paths** — Task `outputPath` is the planned output directory and can be null. Gallery `folder` is the registered directory. Path separators can differ. Join records by work ID.
- **Times** — Task `updatedAt` uses ISO 8601 and can include fractional seconds. Batch `createdTime`, gallery `time` and schedule `nextRunTime` use Unix milliseconds. Send the history cursor’s `beforeTime` back with its full precision.
- **Response bodies** — `GET /api/authors` returns an array. `GET /api/authors/paged` returns the array in `content` with pagination metadata. `GET /api/downloaded/statistics` returns an object with `success` and counts.
- **Reading an illustration** — Use `GET /api/library/artworks/{artworkId}` for the download record and optional file verification (missing record: empty 400). Use `GET /api/gallery/artwork/{artworkId}` for visible gallery metadata (404 if unavailable). The local interface uses `GET /api/downloaded/{artworkId}`; program keys use the library route.
- **Filters** — Gallery queries use comma-separated values, for example `?format=jpg,png&collectionIds=12,34`. An export request uses JSON arrays inside `filter`, for example `{"formats":["jpg","png"],"collectionIds":[12,34]}`.

### Pagination and continuation

messages.integration:
Use `GET /api/security/program-keys/self` to read this key’s grants. Poll `GET /api/download/tasks` or an individual task for `phase`, `updatedAt` and `revision`. When the worker reports counts, `progress` gives the unit, completed count and total. Download event streams require a session. Start polling every 2 seconds. If `revision` stays the same, increase the interval up to 10 seconds. Return to 2 seconds after an update. Stop when `phase` is `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED`. If a response includes `Retry-After`, wait at least that long before the next request.

The `x-csrf-origin` rule on a write operation also applies to Bearer clients. `origin-or-referer` requires a same-origin Origin or Referer. For `origin-required`, send an Origin that meets the operation’s requirements.

By default, a web page can call the API directly only from the same origin (scheme, host and port). Pages on other origins can send requests through their own backend. The OpenAPI server URL `/` is the root of the origin serving this document. Configure the full instance URL in standalone clients.
messages.intro: Create a program key on the desktop Security page. Send it over HTTPS in the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header. You can test requests here over HTTPS or on loopback. The OpenAPI operation’s `responses[status].links` describe follow-up requests. Open `externalDocs` for the guide. Use `x-related-operations` to discover related methods, then check the target operation and permissions before calling it. `x-related-guides` lists guides linked by those operations.

messages.missing:
### When a record is missing

| Resource | Response | Client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local download record `GET /api/library/artworks/{artworkId}` | `400` | The body is empty. Check status and body before parsing JSON. |
| Partial download record `GET /api/library/artworks/{artworkId}/partial` | `404 error.request.not-found` | There is no unfinished page selection for this artwork. |
| Download task UUID `GET /api/download/tasks/{taskId}` | `404 DOWNLOAD_TASK_NOT_FOUND` | Check the receipt and caller identity. Unknown and invisible tasks give the same error. |
| Download progress by artwork `GET /api/download/status/{artworkId}` | `200 success=false` | There is no visible progress record. |
| Archive status `GET /api/archive/status/{token}` | `200 status=expired` | The token is unknown or expired. Stop polling. |
| Archive file `GET /api/archive/download/{token}` | `410` | Request a new archive if the file is still needed. |

messages.pagination:
Pagination depends on the endpoint. `GET /api/gallery/artworks` uses `page` and `size`, starting at page 0. `GET /api/download/batches/{id}/items` uses `offset` and `limit`. For `GET /api/download/tasks/history`, omit `beforeTime` and `beforeId` on the first request. To continue, send both values returned by the previous page.

The plugin market uses `cursor` and `limit`. Omit `cursor` on the first request. For the next page, set `cursor` to `nextCursor` from `/api/plugin-market/catalog` or `nextVersionCursor` from `/api/plugin-market/plugins/{repositoryId}/{pluginId}`. Pixiv artwork and novel searches and series lookups take only `page` for pagination, starting at 1. The followed-creators feed uses p. Range searches use startPage and endPage.
messages.permissions:
Each operation lists its route policy, authentication alternatives and permissions. Some also check the target plugin. Administrators can list permissions at GET /api/security/program-keys/permissions. Send the Bearer key by itself, without a session or invitation cookie, X-Session-Token or X-GUI-Token. Routes under /api/gui/ serve the local desktop. Program clients should choose an operation that declares programKey and use its documented response. See the top-level `x-program-permission-conditions` for the phases, fields and context expressions used in `x-program-permissions`. A valid Bearer key sent on its own to an operation without `programKey` receives `403 auth.program.unsupported`, even when anonymous access is allowed. An invalid key or mixed credentials can return `401 auth.program.invalid`.

To rotate a key, an administrator creates its replacement on the desktop Security page or through an administrator session. Switch the client, verify the new identity and grants with `GET /api/security/program-keys/self`, then have the administrator revoke the old key. Tasks submitted with the old key remain scoped to it. Finish polling them before revocation or follow them with an administrator session.
